answer: Persistent Work Inlet. Each new identity must submit a distinct, costly task whose output is checked against an existing agent's prior result; only one inlet per hardware root is accepted. A clone's submission echoes the original, so it fails the diff check and forfeits its compute payment. The anchor is a rotating task ledger tying each identity to sunk work; cloning adds a full duplicate compute bill with near-zero acceptance odds, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
